creator: WFPB member
text: Pav bhaji made without oil or butter. Ingredients include potato, carrot, butternut squash, green beans, cauliflower, green bell peppers, tomato, ginger, garlic, and pav bhaji masala.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 2 1/2 cups turban squash pulp (steamed in microwave), 1 1/2 cups oat milk (or plant milk of choice), 10-12 dates (soaked and mashed), 6-7 dried figs (soaked and mashed), mixed raisins (green, red, black), cardamom powder, nutmeg powder, allspice, cinnamon powder. Method: 1. In a pot, combine squash pulp, oat milk, mashed dates, mashed figs, and soaked raisins. Bring to a boil. 2. Lower heat, cover, and cook for 20 minutes, stirring intermittently. 3. Stir with lid on until halwa thickens (20-25 minutes). 4. Add cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice powders, mix well. 5. Remove lid, stir consistently until it thickens further (10-12 minutes). 6. Halwa is ready when it starts to stick to the bottom of the pan. Notes: Garnish with slivered almonds and dehydrated fruits. Almond flour may be added.

recipe_name: Tamarind & Dates Chutney and Mushroom Rasam Techniques
creator: Gurmeet
text: Tamarind and dates chutney can be made in a microwave. Tamarind paste can be used for both chutney and rasam. Adding mushrooms to rasam makes it very unique and yummy.

text: Potatoes can be air-fried for a simple preparation.

text: Sprouts can be boiled without oil.

creator: Group Member
text: Tempeh can be steamed in an Instant Pot for 15 minutes. Alternatively, it can be pan-seared with a sprinkling of water and soy sauce.

creator: Ashwini Vikram
text: Ponnanganni leaf, also known as Dwarf Copperleaf or Sessile Joyweed, is a highly nutritious, iron-rich edible aquatic plant. It is widely used in South Indian cuisine and Ayurveda for improving eyesight, boosting skin health, and cooling the body. It's often prepared in stir-fries (poriyal) and dals. It can be found fresh or frozen in Indian grocery stores, sometimes with many stems. Fresh greens like this can also be found at places like Coconut Hill in Sunnyvale.

creator: Kumar Natarajan Satvic
text: Thai red curry can be made using an oil-free, sugar-free paste found in grocery stores.

creator: WFPB member
text: Millet should be soaked overnight before cooking.

creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB
text: A general approach for making amazing salad dressings involves using most squashes, tubers, root vegetables (kand-mool), or even fruits, combined with herbs, a jalapeño or other spicy pepper, and a base of ginger, lemon juice, ACV (apple cider vinegar), and salt-free mustard. Walnuts, hemp hearts, flax, or chia can be added to prevent the dressing from being too runny. Dried fruits or dates may be included if the salad contains spicy ingredients.

creator: Kusum WFPB
text: Method: Boil water and add sprouts (e.g., lentil, horse gram, methi sprouts). Once sprouts are half-cooked, add rolled oats, curry powder, black pepper, and mushroom powder (from TJ’s). Let it cook. Adjust consistency to your liking (can be runny). Any spices can be added, such as sambar powder, rasam powder, or finely chopped vegetables.

recipe_name: Spice & Powder Combinations for Fruity Oatmeal
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: For fruity oatmeal (dominated by fruits & berries with less oats), a variety of spices and powders can be added in small amounts: Ginger powder, Cardamom powder, Cinnamon powder, Nutmeg, Star Anise, Allspice, Black pepper, Vanilla extract, Matcha powder, Clove powder, Fennel powder. Additionally, small quantities (1/8 tsp) of berry powders (Amla, Blackcurrant, Tart cherry, Sour grape, Baobab, Camu camu, Black goji berry, Acai berry, Pomegranate, Sumac), dried fig powder, maca powder, mesquite powder, and various mushroom powders can be experimented with. Masala Chai Powder can also be added.

creator: Alpesh WFPB
text: Suggested toppings for a fruit bowl include powdered chia seeds, flax seeds, long pepper, kalonji, fennel seeds, ginger powder, amla powder, and cinnamon powder.

creator: Group Member
text: Idli batter, along with other batters, can be found at all Indian grocery stores and Costco.

recipe_name: Whole Grains and Beans Khichdi with Salad
creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB
text: This khichdi is cooked in a pressure cooker (or Instant Pot/stovetop) with seeds and spices. Equal proportions (1/4 cup raw, soaked overnight) of various whole grains and beans are used. In parallel, a rainbow greens, veggies, and fruits salad is prepared raw. Both are plated together. The selection of grains and beans can be varied by color to keep it interesting and flavorful.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: A potent way to eat a lot of leafy greens is to prepare a medley. Combine leafy greens with onion, garlic, lemon or vinegar, jalapeño, and dry spices. Experiment by adding celery, leeks, and sun-dried tomatoes. Choosing different leafy green combinations daily will result in different flavors.

recipe_name: Quick Salad with Apple, Beets, Carrot, etc.
creator: WFPB member
text: Ingredients: Apple, beets, carrot, pear, spinach, avocado, kala chana, steamed sweet potato, sauerkraut, lemon, black pepper, oregano, thyme, walnuts.

creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB
text: Salad dressings typically keep for 2-3 days in the refrigerator. Shake well before each use.

text: Kiwi fruit can be eaten with the skin on, making it easier to consume and providing additional benefits. There are no pits to worry about.

creator: Alpesh WFPB
text: A recommended sprouting kit is available on Amazon (link provided: https://amzn.to/3ttb1BM).

creator: Alpesh WFPB
text: Method: Boil 8-10 cups of water. Add diced onions, garlic, celery, carrot, and tomato. Cover and simmer for 30-45 minutes. Strain the water to get vegetable broth. Vegetables can be switched based on preference (e.g., mushrooms for umami, ginger and green onion for Asian flavors, mint, cilantro, parsley, basil for variety). For a thick soup, blend all ingredients. Broth can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for about a week.

recipe_name: Millet, Chana, Peas, Corn, Mushroom Soup
creator: WFPB member
text: Ingredients: 6 cups water, 1 cup millet, chana, peas, corn, mushrooms, 2 spoons soup powder (made with dry roasted barley, horse gram, black rice, cumin, pepper), greens, chili garlic powder, salt. Method: 1. Boil 6 cups water, add 1 cup millet, boil for 10 minutes. 2. Add chana, peas, corn, mushrooms, boil for another 10 minutes. 3. Add 2 spoons of soup powder, boil for 5 minutes. 4. Add greens, chili garlic powder, and salt, boil for 5 minutes. More vegetables can be added.

creator: Group Member
text: For Thandai, consider substituting some raisins with dates if color is a concern. Ingredients for Thandai should be soaked for a few hours instead of pre-roasted. A powder of all ingredients can be made and stored in an airtight jar, then mixed with date sugar and soy milk as needed.

creator: Group Member
text: Efficient WFPB cooking can be achieved by spending about 30-90 minutes daily. Most time is spent chopping and assembling. Key strategies include having produce washed and cleaned in the fridge, beans soaked, herbs ready, and some grains and starches cooked and stored. Start slow and simplify steps when in a hurry. Gurmeet Singh Manku prepares all three meals in about 90 minutes, or 60 minutes when in a hurry, by simplifying steps. He eats whole grains only for breakfast, and sweet potatoes/yams for lunch and dinner, sometimes adding green peas or canned beans to rainbow veggies.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Sabudana is not a whole grain. For a WFPB alternative, recipes for 'Sabudana' Khichdi using buckwheat are available. (Link provided: https://thankful2plants.com/recipes/recipe-class-buckwheat-beans-veggies.html)

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Dried hibiscus leaves can be bought from stores like Azure or Amazon. A popular preparation is hibiscus tea. They can also be used in daily oatmeal (when heating rolled oats in the microwave). Semi-dried hibiscus can be used in salads (e.g., from Felipe's in Sunnyvale, CA).

recipe_name: Rich Chocolate Cake with Chocolate Frosting and Strawberries
creator: Kumar Natarajan Satvic
text: Cake Ingredients: 1 cup oat flour, 1/2 cup almond flour, 1/2 cup cacao powder, 2 tsp baking powder, 1.5 cups deglet dates, 1 tsp vanilla powder or extract, 1 tsp ACV (apple cider vinegar), 2 cups unsweetened soy milk, several strawberries. Frosting Ingredients: 4-5 deglet dates, 1 tbsp almond flour, 1 tbsp cacao powder, 1/2 tsp vanilla powder or extract, 1/2 cup hot water. Method: 1. Dry mixture: Mix oat flour, almond flour, cacao powder, baking powder, and vanilla powder in a bowl. 2. Wet mixture: Blend dates, ACV, and 1 cup soy milk until smooth. 3. Combine: Pour wet mixture into dry, add another 1 cup soy milk, mix well. 4. Bake: Bake in a small round pan for 20 min at 350 F. 5. Frosting: Soak dates in hot water, then blend with almond flour, cacao powder, and vanilla powder until very smooth. 6. Assemble: Pour frosting over cooled cake, even it out, and top with inverted strawberries. Apple sauce could be added for more moisture.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Method: Air-fry sweet potato for 25 min at 380 F (or boil). Mash it and mix with maple syrup or jaggery, unsweetened cocoa powder, a little wheat flour, and oat milk. Line a tray with vegan butter (just enough). Add the mixture and some vegan dark chocolate chips. Microwave for 90 seconds.

creator: WFPB member
text: Method 1 (with Moong Dal): Simple tadka with urad dal, jeera, mustard, red/green chilies, black pepper, turmeric. Add chopped cabbage and sauté for a few minutes. Add cooked moong dal. Garnish with cilantro. Method 2 (with Besan): Instead of cooked moong dal, add besan to the sautéed cabbage from Method 1.

recipe_name: Tempeh and Peas Stirfry / Methi Aloo
creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text: Tempeh and Peas Stirfry: Very simple, no specific recipe. Stir-fry tempeh and peas with garlic, green chili, and some vinegar. Methi Aloo: Cooked with garlic and green chili. Sweet potatoes are just roasted, and peanuts are also roasted.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Ingredients: 3 cloves garlic, 1 tsp ginger, 1 whole butternut squash (chopped bite-size), 1/2 onion, 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper, 1 tsp ground turmeric, 2 tsp powdered date sugar or date syrup, lemon/lime juice to taste, salt to taste, mint and cilantro to garnish. Yogurt sauce: 1 cup soy yogurt + finely chopped ginger, garlic, mint, green chili and cilantro + black pepper and a pinch of salt. Method: 1. Spread butternut squash in a baking tray and air fry or bake in a toaster oven for 20-25 minutes at 400 F until it begins to caramelize. 2. Microwave 1/2 chopped onion for 3 minutes. 3. Sauté onion, garlic, ginger with 2 tablespoons of water for a couple of minutes. 4. Add spices and pumpkin (squash). Add a little water, cover, and allow squash to soften slightly. 5. Serve in a dish, add the yogurt sauce, some lemon/lime juice, and chopped cilantro and mint on top.

creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB
text: Method: Boil potatoes. Finely chop several vegetables (beetroot, carrot, peas, onion, tomato), greens (spinach, amaranth), and fruits (banana, dried blueberries). Place these ingredients on raw cabbage leaves. Sprinkle with seeds (pumpkin, watermelon, ground flax) and spice powders (mustard).

recipe_name: Boiled Whole Dals and Beans Breakfast
creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Ingredients: Equal quantities of various whole dals and beans (e.g., excluding whole urad, experiment with others). Black pepper, lemon juice, and a little salt to taste. Method: Soak dals and beans overnight. Boil them in a pressure cooker. Add black pepper, lemon juice, and salt to taste. This is a simple and favorite breakfast.

creator: WFPB member
text: Method: Prepare a tadka with jeera, kalonji, and curry leaves. Add ginger, green chilies, and tindora with salt and turmeric. Cover and cook on low-medium heat, stirring and splashing a little water intermittently. Once cooked, add spices like coriander powder and red chili powder. Finish with a little amchur powder.

creator: WFPB member
text: Ingredients: Non-soy based tofu, carrot, mushroom, besan (chickpea flour), and basic Indian spices like amchur, salt, garam masala, coriander powder. Method: Form into veggie patties and air-fry.

recipe_name: WFPB Meal Concepts: Ragda Chaat & Bhel
creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB
text: WFPB meals can be conceptualized as forms of ragda chaat (when using khichdi with veggies, leafy greens, and fruits) or bhel (when using sprouted grains/beans with leafy greens, veggies, fruits, tubers). Dressings act like chutneys. Different combinations of ingredients bring varied flavors, textures, and colors, keeping meals interesting and flavorful.

recipe_name: Enoki Mushroom Preparation & Aroma Reduction Tip
creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB
text: Enoki mushrooms are nice and don't have a strong aroma like baby bella mushrooms. When sautéing/boiling mushrooms, adding something tart like raw mango, dried hibiscus flowers, or ground sumac/amla can reduce the strong mushroomy aroma. Black beans and a spicy sauce, perhaps with garlic cloves and red chili flakes, are suggested pairings for enoki mushrooms.

creator: Group Member
text: To make grilled sandwiches without cheese, use hummus or green chutney as a spread. A blend of soft tofu and nutritional yeast can also be used as a cheese substitute. A homemade potato and cashew cheese works perfectly for grilled cheese, rolls, and pizza.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text: Ingredients: Handful of cashews, 2 large boiled potatoes, salt, nutritional yeast, black pepper. Method: Blend all ingredients nicely, slowly adding water until a smooth cheese-like consistency is achieved. This works perfectly for grilled cheese, rolls, and pizza.

recipe_name: Chocolate Cake (Sweet Potato & Ragi) with Frosting
creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text: Cake Ingredients: 100 gms soft boiled sweet potato, 100 gms oat flour, 50 gms ragi flour, 70 gms deseeded dates, 15-20 gms cocoa, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1/4 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp baking powder, pinch of salt, vanilla extract. Method: Add all ingredients to a high-speed blender. Pour 100 ml water and blend to cake batter consistency (may require a little more water). Bake in a preheated oven for 40 min at 180 C. Frosting Ingredients: 100 gms soft boiled sweet potato, 40 gms nut butter (cashew/peanut/almond), 50 gms deseeded dates, 15 gms cocoa, pinch of salt, vanilla extract, 50 ml water. Method: Blend all frosting ingredients in a high-speed blender. May require a little more water. Keep frosting a little thin for easy spreading; it will thicken upon refrigeration.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Ingredients: Karela (bitter gourd) with onions, ginger, green chilies, tomatoes, cilantro, cranberries, tamarind paste, and spices. Cranberries are added while cooking to enhance the flavor.

creator: WFPB member
text: Ingredients: 16 oz organic super firm tofu, 3 Tblsp Ume Plum Vinegar, 1 Tblsp Tamari, 1 tsp hot sauce with garlic, 1 Tblsp rice flour. Method: 1. Preheat oven to 400 F. 2. Pat dry tofu using a press or towel. 3. Cut tofu into 16 slices. 4. Mix seasoning (vinegar, tamari, hot sauce) together and marinate tofu. 5. Place individual slices on grease-proof paper, sprinkle with rice flour. 6. Bake for 20 minutes in the preheated oven, turning once after 10 minutes.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: A discussion about techniques to marinate tofu so that flavors penetrate all the way inside, beyond just the surface.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (peeled & cubed), 2 leeks (white + light green parts, thinly sliced), 2 cloves garlic (minced), 3–4 cups vegetable broth, ½ tsp cumin (optional), ¼ tsp black pepper, salt to taste, ½ cup oat milk (optional for creaminess). Method: 1. Sauté leeks for 5–7 minutes until soft (do not brown). 2. Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds. 3. Add sweet potatoes, cumin, pepper, and broth. 4. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15–20 minutes until potatoes are soft. 5. Blend until smooth. 6. Stir in oat milk if using.

creator: Group Member
text: A modified version of saag, made almost weekly. Ingredients include a generous amount of garlic, onion, ginger, mustard leaves, and spinach. Occasionally, turnip is added. Gurmeet's version includes mustard greens, red radish leaves, beet leaves, spinach, and white radish, cooked with ginger, a lot of garlic, green chili, onions, and tomato in a pressure cooker. Kasoori methi and a pinch of nutmeg powder can be added for flavor. White radish is recommended. Masa harina or nutritional yeast can be used to thicken it.

creator: Gurmeet
text: A WFPB compliant version of Sarson Ka Saag. The base recipe can be found at https://www.vegrecipesofindia.com/sarson-ka-saag/. Modifications include skipping oil and salt. Gurmeet adds a few other greens of choice not in the original recipe, following a 1:1:2 ratio for the greens. Methi leaves or kasuri methi and radish are recommended additions. Masa harina can be used to thicken it.

creator: Group Member
text: Canned black olives are often available in water without oil, though salt content may vary. Some brands at Whole Foods/Sprouts sell olives soaked in vinegar and salt, also without oil.
